_readme: OFFICIAL PLANNING / PERMIT SYSTEMS, per jurisdiction, recorded whether or not HomeSignal reads them (2026-11-12).
Why: source discovery used to look only at a jurisdiction's open-data catalog, so a city whose catalog has no
permit dataset was recorded as having no permit records (Oakland CA, docs/source-registry.md 'Alameda CA' row),
while the city runs a public planning and permit portal. A missing catalog dataset is not a missing record system.
Every state below is a fact about what WE checked, never a claim about what the jurisdiction holds:
discovery_state  not_investigated | portal_found | automated_search_verified | manual_only | access_restricted | integrated
Record coverage and document coverage are separate: a working search does not prove bulk access or attachments.
Each check carries the date, the URL, what came back and the method. A finding of 'no matching record' names the
query and the sources checked; it never says that no application exists.
Validated by test/official-record-portals.test.mjs. Pure data: adding a jurisdiction is adding an entry.

open_data_catalog.finding: No permit or planning ledger in the catalog (docs/source-registry.md, Alameda CA row). Not re-checked 2026-11-12.

portals.access_notes: Anonymous GET of the global search returns a results page (10 rows a page). Record numbers are links that run an ASP.NET postback, so a search result carries no stable per-record URL; record detail and attachments were not opened. Not integrated: no connector reads this portal.

supplementary.finding: HTTP 403 'Access Denied' to the database's outbound HTTP (pg_net request 23491, 2026-11-12). Not worked around.
HTTP 204 with no body to pg_net (request 23518, 2026-11-12); the request system was not examined further.
